title: R' Simon bar Zevadi (or Zevid)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman states that he was a student of R' Ila, as in Pesachim ch. 8 halakha 6: "He taught before R' Hila," and in Sukkah ch. 2 halakha 8: "He raised an objection before R' Ila."

Likewise Hyman records that he posed a question before R' Yosi (R' Assi), as in Shevi'it ch. 2 halakha 8.
And he studied with the sons of R' Yosa, as in Shabbat ch. 7 halakha 1, on the testimony of R' Hizkiya.
And he disagrees with R' Shmuel bar Nachmani, as in Pesachim beginning of ch. 9, Nedarim ch. 6 halakha 13.

Likewise it is mentioned in Pesachim ch. 9 halakha 1 that he said: the skull of Arnan the Jebusite was found by them under the altar; and in Sotah ch. 7 halakha 5 he said: "And it is fitting: if you say [supplied אין תימי] the stones of the lodging place..."
Those who transmit in his name we find to be R' Hizkiya, R' Yona, R' Pincham, as in Kohelet Rabbah beginning of ch. 2.
Hyman states that he died in the presence of his teacher R' Ila, as in Berakhot ch. 2 halakha 8 and Horayot ch. 3 halakha 5: thus, R' Simon bar Zevid died; R' Lia entered (and in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 91 sec. 9 it reads R' Ala, and in Kohelet Rabbah 5:11 it reads R' Ila; Hyman says that this is one name, as is known) and eulogized him: we have lost R' Simon; who will bring us his replacement? And R' Levi likewise eulogized him and said: the tribes found a find and their heart failed them; we who have lost R-S bar Zevid—all the more so.

notes.text: Hyman’s proposed Yosi/Assi and Ila/Hila/Lia/Ala equivalences remain his claims, without authority merging. The Sotah wording אין תימי and the compressed tribal-find eulogy remain difficult; “all the more so” at the end is not an empty etc.

The whole saved Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Sotah chapter7 scalar, text index4/subindex2 (640 characters), was read and checked against its raw SHA256, selector and actual edition metadata. It explicitly names Rabbi Simon bar Zevid locally, then reads ויאות אין תימר אבני המלון. That supports the conditional sense IF YOU SAY, beside supplied אין תימי, without changing the supplied Hebrew, asserting a misprint or reconstructing a printed correction history. The abbreviated supplied clause ends at the stones of the lodging place; the scalar's subsequent explanations, three/four kinds of stones, other figures and Jordan conclusion are not imported. The earlier IF NOT rendering stays exact in history. The full Rabbi in this Sotah scalar supports only its own local Simon occurrence; it supplies no full title to the heading, the Pesachim/Sukkah/Sheviit/Shabbat speakers, Kohelet transmitters or eulogists. Unsupported titles therefore remain R'. The source heading's Zevadi OR Zevid is retained, not harmonized. Ila/Hila/Lia/Ala remain separate literal forms; Hyman's parenthesis says ONE NAME, AS IS KNOWN, and this definite assertion is expressly attributed rather than weakened into a possibility or admitted as an authority identity. Yosi (Assi) remains his parenthetical alternative, with Yosa distinct and no identity or chronological merger. The source Pincham פנחם is retained rather than silently substituting the older Pinchas; Arnan ארנן remains the supplied Jebusite form beside historical Araunah, without claiming a biblical emendation. The source's שן in the skull clause is not changed; the inherited OF interpretation is contextual, not a new Pesachim witness. Hyman's student/teacher, taught-before, objected-before, asked-before, studied WITH the SONS, testimony, disagreement, transmitters-IN-HIS-NAME and death-before-his-teacher claims retain their directions as source claims, not genealogy or chronology admission. BEFORE in the quotations does not itself establish a date or authority binding. All source locators, including Pesachim8hal6/9hal9/BEGINNING9, Sukkah2hal8, Sheviit2hal8, Shabbat7hal1, Nedarim6hal13, BEGINNINGKohelet2, Berakhot2hal8, Horayot3hal5, BR91section9 and Kohelet5section11, remain conventional interpretations without fresh named-edition verification of those passages. In the eulogy, WE LOST/WHO WILL BRING US/A REPLACEMENT keeps first-person plural and the genuine question. The compressed tribal-find clause preserves the supplied ויצא לכם as and it went out to you, with its difficult sense unresolved; the older they-lost-it interpretation remains exact in history, not a newly verified Hebrew reading. WE WHO HAVE LOST and ALL THE MORE SO retain their emphatic force. Final R-S bar Zevid leaves the initials unexpanded; contextual Simon in the old note and English remains historical without identity admission. No missing eulogy story, scriptural quotation or answer is imported. The three original mixed notes and current mixed note, all old English and every root intermediate are preserved exactly; the proposed current-note revision and proposed source-question resolution are not applied. Only this qualification is appended, and p003 remains held with no publication, canonical change, note retirement or semantic/authority admission.

The whole printed notice is in volume III, p. 964. It gives Pesachim 9:1 (ה״א), של in the skull phrase, תמורתו (“his replacement”), and ויצא לבם (“their heart went out”), beside the frozen Hebrew’s 9:9 (ה״ט), שן, תמורתנו and ויצא לכם. The English follows these printed readings, rendering the last phrase “their heart failed them”; the Hebrew and existing notes remain unchanged. The whole consulted Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim chapter 9, first halakhah, directly names Simon bar Zavdi and the skull of Ornan the Jebusite. Arnan remains the supplied name in the translation, without replacing it by the older Araunah. The whole Berakhot 2:8 passage has Lai and the replacement eulogy, followed by Levi’s comparison with Joseph’s brothers, whose heart failed them when they found the money; Horayot 3:5 has Hilay and the same comparison. Those different names do not establish Hyman’s Ila/Hila/Lia/Ala equivalence or prove his teacher and death chronology. His definite “one name, as is known” remains expressly attributed. The whole consulted Sotah passage has אין תימר, “if you say,” beside supplied אין תימי; the following stone discussion is not inserted. Yosi/Assi remains Hyman’s alternative, Yosa remains distinct, Pincham and final R-S are retained, and no person or family identity is newly admitted. The exact other named editions remain uncollated here. All existing notes are preserved verbatim.
